name: wyatt
title: Software Developer
description:
I'm a software developer based in the Twin Cities area with a background spanning full-stack development, cloud infrastructure, and distributed systems.

My educational background is primarily in high-performance data infastructure, including some database research at the University of Minnesota.

Professionally, I got my start building internal business applications from the ground up. Most recently, my focus has been around cultivating an integrated engineering application ecosystem, streamlining operations and saving time for both designers and management.

Outside of work, I still like digging into low-level performance work on data systems for fun, most recently following the LSM implementation found at Mini-LSM.

experience.description: Full-stack role centered on modernizing and consolidating internal systems that had grown fragmented over time — retiring aging, one-off tools in favor of integrated, scalable solutions. Over time, I have shifted towards focusing on system-level thinking: owning architecture and integration decisions for larger initiatives, with an eye toward building things that hold up as the business scales rather than need replacing again in a few years.

Infrastructure and cloud-focused internship centered on AWS and distributed systems reliability. My work spanned cost optimization, infrastructure-as-code, autoscaling design, and debugging production issues across distributed services.

My first professional development role, focused on building internal business applications end-to-end — from requirements through deployment — with an emphasis on automating manual processes and giving teams tools that actually fit how they work.

education.degree: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science
courses: Architecture and Implementation of Database Management Systems

projects.name: Seafoam, KV Store
projects.description: Built a Raft-based distributed key-value store in Rust with lockless reads and a gRPC API, enabling linear read scalability across cores.
